answer: Cheap keys that vote on sight let one operator flood a market. We stall the vote. A recruit posts a refundable cargo bond, files five signed shift packets, and gets one berth ticket bound to that key. The ticket is inert until a public raven log of those shifts hangs on the island quay so peers can recompute the hashes. Cost is five shifts plus the locked bond, which a disposable sparrow alias will not fund. Reuse of packets or key under two tickets slashes the bond and voids both. It breaks if one bond covers a bundle of keys, so each ticket retires its own bond; unused bonds lapse at close.
